name: Gratian compiles the Decretum
summary: The Camaldolese monk Gratian, teaching at Bologna, compiles the Concordia Discordantium Canonum, the systematic harmonisation of canon law that becomes universally known as the Decretum. It is the first part of what later became the Corpus Iuris Canonici, the basis of medieval canon law down to 1917.

_quarry.structural_significance: Foundation of medieval canon law; Bologna's law school's authority across Latin Christendom derives in large part from Gratian's systematisation of conflicting canons by dialectical method.
